content.title: Route per-kind Turn behavior through turnBehavior
content.intent: This PR refactors per-kind Turn behavior into one table, turnBehavior, so prompt mode, tool access, delivery and the Automation gate stop branching on scattered Run fields.

chapters.label: One table for Turn behavior
chapters.caption: Per-kind decisions that were spread across the runtime now come from one lookup.
chapters.body: Before this PR, what a Turn could do (its prompt mode, its tools, whether it must end with finishAutomationRun) was decided in many places, each reading a different signal: the Agent invocation id, the Automation result flag, a root-kind check, or a Thread-only subagents flag. This PR puts those answers in one table [1] keyed by Conversation kind, person input, and Automation run, and a source check blocks new branches elsewhere. The PR says no behavior change; the review risk is Event Turns on child Conversations, which the new key routes differently.

evidence.note: The selector every caller now reads

chapters.label: The behavior table
chapters.caption: Four fixed rows cover a root, a person in a Thread, an agent in a child, and an Automation run.
chapters.body: Each row (`TurnBehavior`) sets where the final response goes, the prompt mode, whether the Turn is gated on an answer tool, and seven tool flags [1]. A person in a Thread is a root row with no agent tools; any other child Turn gets reportBlocked instead of the review desk, subscriptions, and user customization [2]. The selector checks the Automation flag first, then root, then person input, and throws for a person's input on a task [3]. The Automation flag is a stated temporary bridge until a Conversation kind for automations exists.
asks: Why does an Automation run keep the root's agent tools?
What replaces automationRun when kind automation ships?

chapters.label: Picking a row per Run
chapters.caption: The agent executor reads the stored kind, the Source, and the dispatch once, then hands the row to the prompt and the gate.
chapters.body: The executor now builds the row from the stored Conversation kind, defaulting to root when no row exists, and refuses to run a child that has no row [1]. The result gate reads `gated` instead of the dispatch flag [2], and the prompt takes its mode from the row instead of re-deriving it from the dispatch and the invocation id [3]. For Agent invocations and person Turns the mapping matches the old derivation.

decisions.claim: A child Run with no Conversation row should fail instead of running with an unknown kind.
decisions.concern: Any child path that runs before its row is written now errors on every attempt; before, it ran with root-like behavior.

asks: Can a root still run before its row exists?

chapters.label: Tools read turnTools
chapters.caption: Agent tools are bound in tool wiring from the row, and tool gates read flags instead of the invocation id.
chapters.body: The runner no longer binds spawnAgent and messageAgent up front; it passes the binders through the Run environment [2], and tool wiring binds them from the row's agent setting [1]. A child still keeps messageAgent to its parent when too deep to spawn. In tool creation, reportBlocked, noReply and the review-desk disable reason now read the row's flags [3][4]. Tool context now requires these flags (`turnTools`), so every test context had to pass a root row.
asks: Does the production messageAgent binder use the new agents argument?

chapters.label: Event Turns on child Conversations
chapters.caption: A non-person Turn on a Thread or task now gets the child-agent row, not only an Agent invocation.
chapters.body: The old gates keyed off the Agent invocation id, which the mailbox worker never sets, and that worker disabled subagents for every Thread Turn [2]. The new key is kind plus person input, so an Event Turn on a Thread or task falls to the child-agent row [1], which the unit table pins [4]. On a Thread such a Turn now gets spawnAgent and messageAgent; on either kind it gets reportBlocked and the child-agent prompt and loses the review desk and subscriptions. Event delivery to the Location stays root-only [3].

evidence.note: Removed: subagents off for every Thread Turn

decisions.claim: An Event Turn on a Thread or task should get child-agent behavior, including spawnAgent.
decisions.concern: PR claims no behavior change. Old code barred Thread Turns from child agents so results don't report as the wrong Actor; no test runs this path.

asks: Can a Thread receive Event Turns today?
Should Event Turns on a Thread get agents none?

chapters.label: Keeping branches in one module
chapters.caption: A new source rule counts kind, parent-edge, Automation-flag and person-Source branches per file against a baseline.
chapters.body: The architecture check now scans runtime source with regexes for kind comparisons, person-Source checks, reads of the Automation flag, and parent-edge fields used as conditions, skipping comments and the table module [1]. Its tests show which forms count and which do not [2]. A baseline records today's count per file, and a count may only go down [3].

decisions.claim: A regex count with a per-file baseline that only shrinks is enough to keep kind branches in kind-behavior.ts.
decisions.concern: The baseline also absorbs branches this PR adds, such as the new parent-edge throw in agent/index.ts, and regexes miss indirect reads.

chapters.label: How we know it works
chapters.caption: Unit tests pin each row and the agent-tool binding, and an eval checks a person's reply in an Automation thread.
chapters.body: A table test checks every kind and opener pair, the task rejection, and the Automation row [1]. New binding tests show a person's Thread Turn gets no agent tools and a too-deep child keeps messageAgent [2]. The Event automation eval now sends a person's follow-up in the run's thread and expects a delivered reply with no finishAutomationRun [3]. The integration assertion that a person's Thread Run disables subagents was removed [4], so that rule is now covered only at unit level.

decisions.claim: A unit test of bindAgentTools is enough to guard that a person's Thread Turn gets no agent tools.
decisions.concern: No integration test checks the wired tools on a real Thread Run, so a regression in how the executor picks the row would pass.

chapters.label: What to watch after ship
chapters.caption: Two new hard errors and child-agent tool calls from Event Turns show whether the mapping holds.
chapters.body: Watch Sentry for "Child Conversation … has no Conversation row" [1] and "A task Conversation cannot have a person's input" [2]; any count means a path the table did not expect. Also watch for spawnAgent or messageAgent calls on Event Turns in Thread Conversations, which had neither tool before, and reportBlocked calls on Event Turns in any child.
